block.title: The getopt clamp proof follows a reordered pair of loads
block.p: A caller can rewind optind between calls to getopt. Glibc compares its saved last nonoption with optind and keeps the smaller index. The clamp proof now states that result directly. Its caller lends the scanner four named fields of the captured C structure.

In a copy of the captured IR, we moved the check and load of optind ahead of the check and load of the last nonoption. The original proof stopped at the first check. The new proof ran the reordered block without edits. Reversing the comparison then failed at the lemma for signed greater-than.

The symbolic executor could already read four-byte integers. It now recognizes their glibc encoding and can read the bytes it returns from one block in the next. It still stops at the four-byte store. At that point the proof uses the existing store rule and shows that the write preserves the OS invariant.

The file grew from 119 to 161 lines with the named fields and the separate clamp lemma. With the imported interfaces built, the median time for Rocq to check the file in a fresh process grew from 3.48 to 4.50 seconds across three runs of each version.
